summary: West-central Charlottetown between downtown and UPEI: Brighton's old wooden houses and Victoria Park (Government House, the battery, the Kiwanis dairy bar) in the south; 1950s-70s Spring Park suburbs round a big civic block (Colonel Gray, Queen Charlotte Intermediate, the new white Simmons Sports Centre and pool, the new turf field) in the middle; and the University Avenue strip (Spring Park Plaza's green fascia, fast food, the CBC, the experimental farm's institutional row, RCMP HQ) up to Belvedere, with Bell Aliant and seniors' housing toward North River Road. The best-photographed are Simmons, Government House, the dairy bar, CBC, the three schools, the plaza and the Garden Home.

buildings.name: Simmons Sports Centre (new, opened Dec 2, 2024), North River Road
buildings.facts: Replaces the 50-year-old Simmons arena and its 50-year-old outdoor pool. Council approved plans Jan 2022; budget rose from about $25M to $33M (Nov 2023) and came in about $36M. Due to open Oct 14, 2024; a leak in the 18 km of pipe under the ice slab delayed it to Dec 2, 2024 (repairs under warranty). The old arena beside it was demolished in 2024 (some funding was tied to knocking it down before the new one worked). NHL-sized rink seating about 600, six dressing rooms, two-lane walking track upstairs, multi-purpose room. Outdoor six-lane 25 m pool opened June 22, 2025; in Sept 2026 a survey found it 8 to 12 mm too short for Swimming Canada certification, and the builder started fixing it Sept 11, 2026. A $250K naming-rights offer was withdrawn. OSM's footprint has no lidar height, so it is the new building (the 2020 lidar saw the old one).
buildings.look: A tall white box for the rink: white ribbed metal walls with thin dark-grey vertical slot windows in irregular groups, a low-slope light-grey metal roof with a block of solar panels at the north-east end. A lower one/two-storey front block (lobby, change rooms) at its south-west end: flat white roof, walls of grey metal panel with a long band of warm wood (cedar-look) cladding and glass, a glassed atrium entrance under a wood-slat soffit. Inside the doors 'SIMMONS Sports Centre' in silver letters on barnboard wood. The outdoor pool sits in a fenced concrete deck beside the low block (aerial photo: on its south-west side toward the parking lot), with lane ropes, umbrellas and loungers. Parking lot on the west side toward North River Road; Colonel Gray's brown roofs just east; playing fields and the new turf field to the north.

buildings.name: Colonel Gray Senior High School, 175 Spring Park Road
buildings.facts: Senior high (grades 10-12). Simmons rebuilt right beside it (its footprint moved closer to the school). June 2024 Charlottetown police tactical unit staged a mock lockdown there for training. Rezoning (2025-26): Queen Charlotte Intermediate students now feed into Colonel Gray; Stratford's new high school opening next fall moves hundreds of students. 2019 vaping crackdown; 2017 the school removed pop.

Main entrance: a row of grey-framed glass double doors under a wide light-grey concrete/panel band carrying 'COLONEL GRAY SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL' in raised dark-grey capitals. Front faces Spring Park Road (east); a long walk across the front lawn to the doors; a flagpole on the lawn.

Nov 2023 the province committed almost $17M over four years for about 10,000 sq ft more space plus new windows, floors and lighting; a later capital plan says $21M. Roof damaged by Fiona (Sept 2022). Sits beside Simmons and Colonel Gray; the new turf field is next to it.

'MAIN ENTRANCE' on a small gold plaque over glass doors reached by yellow-painted concrete steps. Front faces North River Road (west), with parking along the road.

buildings.name: Spring Park Elementary School, 30 Dunkirk Street
buildings.facts: New school opened 2013 and overcrowded almost from day one: 24 classrooms for 29 homerooms (2018); rezoning of some students to West Royalty Elementary phased in over five years (2019). Oct 2024 the custodians' union said students in some Island schools were being taught in closets and under staircases, Spring Park named. A buddy bench was installed (2016).

The gym block is red brick on its lower part and dark royal-blue ribbed metal above, the blue cut along its bottom edge into a row of house-shaped (pointed gable) notches over the brick; 'SPRING PARK SCHOOL' in white serif letters on the brick corner. Long low classroom wings of grey/white metal panel and light brick with ribbon windows, some yellow accent panels. Entrance under a flat navy-blue box canopy on posts. Front faces Dunkirk Street (west) across a lot; flagpole with the Canadian flag beside the gym.

buildings.name: Government House (Fanningbank), 1 Terry Fox Drive, Victoria Park
buildings.facts: Lieutenant-governor's residence, built 1834 (designer Isaac Smith), wood frame, Georgian/Palladian; land set aside by Governor Fanning (1789). In 1873 16 ha of its farm became Victoria Park. National Historic Site. Gardens reopened to the public 2021. A 2015 NDP proposal to make it a museum went nowhere. The LG's office costs taxpayers about $650K a year (2015 article).
buildings.look: Large white two-storey wooden house, shutters dark green, low hipped roof of grey shingles with four tall red-brick chimneys. Centre front (south, toward the harbour) a two-storey portico of white columns under a pediment, and a one-storey veranda on white columns wrapping the front and sides. Lower white wings at the back. Gravel drive loops to the front; a formal hedged garden (box hedges, roses, peonies) east of the house.

buildings.name: Kiwanis Dairy Bar, Victoria Park (by the boardwalk)
buildings.facts: Run by the Kiwanis Club since 1955; P.E.I.'s oldest operating dairy bar. One operator for over four decades. March 2024 asked the city for $50K toward a $600K expansion (walk-in freezer, storage, staff washroom). Renovated: grand reopening and 70th birthday July 19, 2025 with 70-cent ice cream; first major update since the 1990s. About 22 hard-serve flavours plus soft serve. Proceeds go to children's charities.
buildings.look: Small one-storey stand, bright yellow clapboard with white trim and white corner boards, a front-gabled roof of grey shingles carried forward over a deep open porch on yellow turned posts; serving windows under the porch with white shutters. An oval sign on the gable: an ice-cream cone with 'Kiwanis Dairy Bar, Since 1955' in navy on white. Grey wooden deck with board railing, red-painted metal railing, picnic tables on the grass looking at the harbour.

buildings.name: Holy Redeemer Church (Roman Catholic), 3 Pond Street
buildings.facts: Parish founded 1929 by the Redemptorists (who left in 1975); the present church complex was built in 1964. One of the city's biggest Catholic churches: Christmas Eve masses for up to 1,300. Hosts the annual Police and Peace Officers' Memorial Service (Sept 2023 photos inside). Graffiti spray-painted on it (2000s).
buildings.look: Interior photos: 1960s modern, walls of warm brown brick, sloping wood-lined ceiling, tall narrow coloured-glass slot windows. Exterior (guess from the date and inside): a broad low brown-brick church with a shallow gabled roof of dark shingles or metal, tall slot windows down the sides, a plain bell tower or tall cross at the front, glass entrance doors under a flat canopy facing Pond Street, big parking lot. The Jack Blanchard Family Centre and other parish buildings stand beside it.

neighbourhoods.name: Brighton
neighbourhoods.where: Between Victoria Park (south) and Euston Street/Spring Park Road (north), from Brighton Road and the North River shore (west) to Kent/Pond/West Streets (east); North River Road and Brighton Road run through it
neighbourhoods.look: The city's older well-off west end: two and two-and-a-half storey wooden houses from about 1880-1940 on big treed lots, clapboard and painted wood shingle, steep gables and cross-gables, front verandas, some Queen Anne towers and bay windows; colours white, cream, pale yellow, sage, grey-blue, a few dark red, with white trim and dark grey or black shingle roofs. Large houses along Brighton Road facing the park and the river. Near Spring and Victoria Streets and Villa Avenue it is denser, with 1960s-80s three-storey walk-up apartments (vinyl or brick, flat or low gabled roofs). Mature elms and maples over the streets.

neighbourhoods.name: Spring Park
neighbourhoods.where: North of Euston Street to Belvedere Avenue, between University Avenue (east) and North River Road (west): Spring Park Road, Kirkwood Drive, Pond Street, Dunkirk Street, Queen Street
neighbourhoods.look: 1950s-70s suburb: one-and-a-half storey Cape Cods with dormers, one-storey bungalows and split-levels on modest lots, vinyl or aluminium siding in white, beige, pale yellow, light grey and pale blue, a few with a brick front; dark grey or brown asphalt roofs; paved driveways, small lawns, a tree or two. Scattered three-storey 1970s walk-up apartment blocks (beige brick or vinyl, gabled or flat roofs) near Spring Park Road, Queen Street and the plaza. The schools, the Simmons centre and the fields form a big open block in the middle.

neighbourhoods.name: University Avenue strip (Euston to Belvedere)
neighbourhoods.where: Both sides of University Avenue from Euston Street to Belvedere Avenue
neighbourhoods.look: Mixed commercial: older two-storey houses turned shops and cafes near Euston (siding, gabled/hipped roofs); then the Spring Park Plaza strip with its green fascia, fast-food pads (Dairy Queen, KFC, McDonald's, Tim Hortons), garages (Coast Tire, Carline), the low brick institutional row on the east side (Farm Centre, CBC, the Agriculture research centre, RCMP HQ) with lawns, and the experimental farm's open fields behind. Overhead power lines on wooden poles along the street (the city wants them buried as part of the redesign).

neighbourhoods.name: Belvedere / west of University Avenue at Belvedere
neighbourhoods.where: Belvedere Avenue from University Avenue west to North River Road
neighbourhoods.look: Commercial and service buildings near University (Bell Aliant exchange, offices, Career Development Services at 160 Belvedere), then 1960s-70s bungalows and split-levels, and seniors' housing (Garden Home, Charlotte Court) at North River Road.

current_events.what: Simmons Sports Centre: $25M became $33M became about $36M; due Oct 14, 2024, delayed by a leak in 18 km of under-ice pipe; opened Dec 2, 2024. The old rink was knocked down first because funding required it, so teams had nowhere to skate. A councillor called it 'a new frontier for recreation'.

The new Simmons 25-metre pool (opened June 22, 2025) is 8 to 12 mm short of 25 metres, so it can't be certified for meets; the builder began fixing it Sept 11, 2026. Swimming Canada: there is 'wiggle room' over 25 m, none under.

The $3M lit turf field next to Simmons was due Sept 2026; the U.S. lighting maker found 50% tariffs made U.S. supply unfeasible, so the lights come from China and the field opens spring 2027. Players aging out will never play on the field they campaigned for.

University Avenue redesign (Belvedere to Euston; medians, bike lanes, new lights at Pond Street, buried power lines): unveiled 2021 at almost $15M, $16-17M by 2023, hoped to start 2024, postponed 18 months in March 2024 over burying power lines, 'still years away' Sept 2025 with most money in 2027-28; Jan 2026 the councillor says the Belvedere intersection fix needs 'patience'.
Experimental farm: declared surplus by Ottawa in 2002, then not; Dec 2023 the mayor floated housing on it amid the housing crisis, a councillor said no.
Proposed U-shaped eight-storey, 257-unit apartment building at 503 University Avenue replacing the old Maritime Christian College (sent to public consultation Feb 2024; status unknown).
current_events.where: 503 University Avenue, west side across from UPEI

current_events.what: Browns Court / 505-531 University Avenue: Killam sold the townhouses and apartments across from UPEI in 2023 to a Montreal student-housing company; tenants (Sept 2025) say they were offered cash (e.g. $7,000) to leave; renovated furnished units rent for $2,500-2,800; the landlord says it has 'never renovicted anyone'.
current_events.where: west side of University Avenue across from UPEI

current_events.what: Spring Park Elementary: opened 2013, over capacity from day one; 2024 union says students taught in closets and under stairs.
Queen Charlotte Intermediate: 30 students over capacity, $17M promised Nov 2023 for an addition with no start date; later capital plan says $21M.
The Garden Home has been on a provisional licence since Jan 2022 for not meeting inspection standards; it handled a dementia unit by converting existing beds rather than adding any.
Kiwanis Dairy Bar asked the city for $50K of a $600K renovation (2024); reopened for its 70th with 70-cent cones (July 2025).
Brighton vacant lots near Spring/Victoria/Villa: empty 15 years, city owns two, the third listed at $129,000 which staff thought too much; residents want a community garden (Dec 2024).
CBC P.E.I. renovated rather than rebuilt ($2M, delays 2018-2020); the new radio studio is glassed in by the front door so the public can watch.
